# FDS Draft: ST-1 Startup Sequence and Protection

Values not in your data are marked **[TBD]** and need vendor or process confirmation. They are not invented.

## 1. Scope and Control Split

- **Woodward governor**: speed/load control, overspeed trip logic (electronic), valve positioning, and critical-band avoidance during acceleration.
- **DCS**: auxiliaries (P-11, P-12, M-15, vacuum/condensate, seals), permissives, and the startup step sequencer.
- **Hardwired trip loop**: all trips in Section 3 act on the trip/throttle valve solenoids independently of DCS and governor communication.

## 2. Startup Sequence

### 2.1 Pre-start Permissives (all must be true to start the sequence)

| # | Permissive |
|---|---|
| 1 | No active trip; trip latch reset |
| 2 | Lube oil header PT-210 ≥ 1.5 barg (normal) with P-11 running |
| 3 | P-12 in AUTO and available (DC supply healthy) |
| 4 | Turning gear M-15 engaged and running |
| 5 | Condenser vacuum established, PT-220 below alarm **[TBD]** and well under 0.3 bara |
| 6 | Vibration XT-301/302 and thrust ZT-310 healthy, no alarms |
| 7 | Steam supply conditions within the start envelope **[TBD]** |
| 8 | 52G open, generator excitation ready |

### 2.2 Steps

**Step 0: Lube oil and turning gear**
1. Start P-11. Confirm PT-210 reaches ~1.5 barg.
2. Verify P-12 is in AUTO standby.
3. Engage M-15 **only at zero speed** (zero-speed signal required).
4. Cold start: M-15 must run for at least **2 h** before the roll permissive is released. The DCS timer runs only while M-15 is confirmed running and resets if it stops. A warm or hot restart interval **[TBD, per OEM]**.

**Step 1: Vacuum and seals**
Establish gland sealing and condenser vacuum per Section 2.1 item 5.

**Step 2: Roll-off**
1. Release the roll permissive when the M-15 timer is complete and all permissives are satisfied.
2. M-15 disengages automatically when the turbine speeds up. The engagement mechanism and any disengagement feedback are **[TBD, OEM]**. Roll-off is not permitted without M-15 disengaged confirmation.
3. The governor accelerates to 500 rpm at the ramp rate **[TBD]**.

**Step 3: 500 rpm hold**
- Hold 20 min for a cold start (shorter or skipped for warm/hot per OEM curve **[TBD]**).
- Check vibration, thrust position, differential expansion **[TBD if instrumented]**, and bearing temperatures.

**Step 4: Acceleration through the critical band**
- Accelerate from 500 to 2000 rpm.
- The governor **must pass through 1600–1900 rpm at a minimum rate [TBD] without holding**.
- Speed holds, "hold" commands, and setpoint stops are blocked inside the 1600–1900 rpm band. A hold request inside the band is rejected, and the ramp continues to 2000 rpm.
- If acceleration stalls in the band (rate below minimum), alarm. The operator must either continue the acceleration or lower speed below 1600 rpm.
- Vibration is monitored through the band. Peaks are expected, and the trip limits stay active.

**Step 5: 2000 rpm hold**
- Hold 15 min, then confirm temperatures, vibration, and thrust are stable.

**Step 6: Acceleration to rated speed**
- Accelerate to 3600 rpm at the ramp rate **[TBD]**.
- Verify P-11 vs shaft-driven pump handover. The main shaft-driven pump takes over and PT-210 stays ≥ 1.5 barg. Per OEM, P-11 stays running or is stopped **[TBD]**. If it is stopped, it remains in AUTO standby so it still starts below 1.0 barg.

**Step 7: Synchronization and loading**
1. Excitation on, voltage matched.
2. The auto-synchronizer issues the close command to **52G** when the synchro-check conditions are met: slip, phase angle, and voltage within limits **[TBD]**. Close attempts are time-limited. On timeout, alarm and return to manual or abort.
3. On breaker close, the governor takes a minimum load block **[TBD]**, then loads at the ramp rate **[TBD]** to the target.
4. Step complete when load is stable and all alarms are clear.

**Abort and shutdown**
- Any trip from Section 3 aborts the sequence. Stop valves close, 52G opens by reverse power or trip logic **[TBD]**, and the unit coasts down with lube oil maintained.
- After the turbine stops, the DCS engages M-15 at zero speed. P-11 stays running until the post-shutdown cooldown period completes **[TBD]**.

## 3. Protection

### 3.1 Lube Oil Pressure (PT-210)

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| Normal | ~1.5 barg |
| < 1.0 barg | P-11 auto-starts (if not already running); alarm |
| < 0.7 barg | P-12 (DC) auto-starts; alarm |
| < 0.6 barg | **Turbine trip** |

- Use a **2oo3 transmitter arrangement** for the trip. A single PT-210 as listed is a single point of failure, so confirm whether additional transmitters exist.
- Start thresholds should have reset hysteresis, so pumps don't cycle. Pumps once started are not auto-stopped, only manually.
- **Startup masking**: the 0.6 barg trip is bypassed only during the initial pressurization before the roll permissive. Once the roll permissive is released, the trip is always active.
- Low pressure with M-15 running inhibits turning gear operation.

### 3.2 Overspeed

- **Electronic trip: 110% = 3960 rpm** (Woodward, plus an independent hardwired overspeed module **[TBD]**, typically 2oo3 speed probes).
- **Mechanical bolt: 111% (≈3996 rpm)**, independent backup.
- The 1% gap between them is narrow. Verify against the OEM that the electronic trip is reliable and does not conflict with the bolt, and plan test procedures for both (the mechanical test is normally done with the OEM procedure).
- On trip, close the trip/throttle and control valves, and open the generator breaker.

### 3.3 Shaft Vibration (XT-301/302)

- **Alarm: 75 µm. Trip: 125 µm.**
- Trip logic is **2oo2 per bearing**: both probes on the same bearing must exceed 125 µm.
- The 2oo2 voting favors availability over safety, since one failed probe or a single high-reading probe will not trip. Mitigations:
  - Probe fault detection (OK/not-OK), with alarm on a bad probe.
  - Decide what happens when one probe is faulted: degrade to 1oo1, or alarm with a time limit **[TBD]**.
  - An alarm on one-probe-high (>125 µm) while the other is below is recommended.
- Trip is not inhibited in the critical band. Alarm and trip settings stay the same, per OEM confirmation **[TBD]**.

### 3.4 Axial Thrust Position (ZT-310)

- **Alarm: ±0.4 mm. Trip: ±0.6 mm.**
- Voting **[TBD]**. A 2oo3 on the probe is recommended; if a single probe, the trip needs fault detection.
- Both directions (active and inactive thrust) are handled symmetrically, per OEM zero reference.

### 3.5 Loss of Vacuum (PT-220)

- **Exhaust pressure high trip: 0.3 bara.**
- Alarm at a lower level **[TBD]**, e.g. a start-up permissive limit.
- Voting 2oo3 recommended **[TBD]**.
- Also consider the exhaust hood temperature and low-vacuum load run-back **[TBD]**.

### 3.6 Other Trips (to be confirmed, not in the data)

Manual emergency trip pushbuttons (hardwired), generator protection trip (86G), high bearing temperatures, high condenser level, main steam parameters, loss of governor (watchdog), and trip-valve fail positions.

### 3.7 Trip Summary

| Trip | Setpoint | Voting |
|---|---|---|
| Low lube oil | 0.6 barg | 2oo3 recommended |
| Overspeed (electronic) | 3960 rpm (110%) | 2oo3 recommended |
| Overspeed (mechanical) | 111% | Independent bolt |
| Shaft vibration | 125 µm | 2oo2 per bearing |
| Thrust position | ±0.6 mm | [TBD] |
| High exhaust pressure | 0.3 bara | [TBD] |

### 3.8 Trip Actions and Reset

On any trip: close the stop valves, open 52G, and latch the trip first-out (cause recorded). Lube oil pumps run as required, and M-15 is engaged at zero speed. Reset is allowed only when the cause is cleared, speed is zero, and the operator acknowledges.

## 4. Open Points for Review

1. 52G opening on trip: reverse power vs immediate trip (a standard question for steam turbine generators).
2. Voting arrangement for PT-210, ZT-310, and PT-220 (only vibration is specified).
3. The narrow 110%/111% overspeed margin.
4. The 2oo2 vibration vote and handling of a probe fault.
5. Ramp rates, warm/hot start holds, and the M-15 restart duration.
6. Whether P-11 stays on after the shaft pump takes over.

I can turn this into a step table with transition conditions and timers, or into a cause-and-effect matrix, if useful.
